rationale:
Evidence. The raced best is iteration 4 (score 81.56), per the outcome table: sensors at x = -0.045, -0.0225, 0, 0.0225, 0.045 with y = 0.05, kp 7.0, ki 0.1, kd 0.3, base_speed 1.4, last_direction. Per track it scored 135.7 (oval, progress 0.33), 67.9 (s-bend, progress 0.17) and 41.1 (slalom, progress 0.10). All 60 trials ended off track, with max_error 0.063 m on each track and about one line loss per run. Iteration 5 moved only y to 0.07 and fell to 61.46, so y = 0.07 is rejected and y = 0.05 is restored.

Corrections to the inputs. The entity1 draft and the critiques say iteration 4 used x = ±0.06. The outcome table and the iteration-4 produced design both show ±0.045, so ±0.045 is the raced baseline. The ±0.06 layout was never raced, so I do not carry it forward. The draft's kd 0.6 was attached to the wrong geometry, so it would have confounded the test. The critique's claim that iteration 1 raised kd from 0.3 to 0.8 is also wrong: the history shows a cut from 0.5 to 0.3, and no run has kd 0.8. The kd evidence is therefore weak, and I do not treat it as support for a higher kd.

Change. One variable only: kd 0.3 to 0.6, applied to the raced ±0.045, y = 0.05 design. Everything else is identical (kp 7.0, ki 0.1, base_speed 1.4, last_direction, same wheels, body and mass). I considered the critique's objection that a doubling is large and kept the step at 0.6 because it is the smallest test that can be read against the baseline at 81.56. I rejected kd 1.8 for saturation risk on tape-edge steps.

Pass and fail rules. The keep rule governs: keep kd 0.6 only if max_error falls and steering_oscillation rises by no more than 20 percent. The 0.19 oval oscillation figure is a soft expectation, not a second pass rule, because the baseline is already at 0.1889 and the two rules conflict. If oscillation rises by more than 20 percent, return to kd 0.3. If max_error changes by less than 0.001 m on each track, kd is not the lever for peak error; the next single test is base_speed alone, and a change is judged real only if it exceeds about 0.001 m. Expected: max_error at or below about 0.062 m on the oval and s-bend, line_loss_events at or below 1 per run, and oval progress at or above 0.33.

Completion. No run has finished and base_speed stays at 1.4, so this race does not address the 500-point completion term. completion_time is requested so the next race can show whether runs are slow or stopped. If runs stay on track with completion_time above 3 s, the next single test is base_speed plus 0.1.
